data.name: Rion
data.long_meaning: The name Rion has a Celtic origin, derived from the word 'righ', meaning 'king'. The name symbolizes a strong and powerful ruler. In Christian tradition, it can be associated with the kingly role of Jesus as the King of Kings.
data.spiritual_meaning: Rion represents the spiritual authority and power of God in one's life.

in_hebrew.name: ריון
in_hebrew.meaning: בן נהר, ילד הנהר, שמו של שני ילדים במקרא,
in_hebrew.long_meaning: בן נהר, ילד הנהר, שמו של שני ילדים במקרא, האחד בספר שמות (שמות כ, י), והשני בספר ישעיהו (ישעיהו, כא), שמו עשוי משלוש האותיות 'ר', 'י', ו'ון', אשר מייצגות את המלים 'ר' (ראש), 'י' (עצמות), 'ון' (אצבע), אשר חוזרות ומופיעות בצורה אחרת בשם האל 'יהוה', שמו נשמע כחיבור של שני שמות, 'ריה' ו'ון', שהם שמות של שני נשמות, 'ר' (ראש) ו'יה' (אל), אשר מייצגים את האל 'יהוה' באופן מורכב.

in_greek.name: Ρίων
in_greek.meaning: παιδί του ποταμού, ονομάζει δύο παιδιά στη Βιβλία
in_greek.long_meaning: παιδί του ποταμού, ονομάζει δύο παιδιά στη Βιβλία, το ένα στην Παλαιά Διαθήκη (Σχετικά 5, 9), το δεύτερο στην Καινή Διαθήκη (Ισαΐας 9:1), ο όρος «Ρίων» είναι σύνθετος από τις τρεις γράμματα «Ρ», «Ι», και «Ω», που αντιπροσωπεύουν τις λέξεις «Ρ» (κέφαλος), «Ι» (σπονδυλική στήλη), και «Ω» (αγκών), που επαναλαμβάνονται με διαφορετική μορφή στο όνομα του Θεού «Ιησούς», ο όρος «Ρίων» ακούγεται ως συνδυασμός των δύο ονομάτων «Ριών» και «Ων», τα οποία είναι ονοματεπώνυμα για δύο ψυχές, «Ρ» (κεφάλι) και «Ιη» (Θεός), που αντιπροσωπεύουν τον Θεό «Ιησούς» με μια πιο σύνθετη μορφή.

in_latin.name: Rion
in_latin.meaning: filius fluminis, duo nomen in libris sanctis
in_latin.long_meaning: filius fluminis, duo nomen in libris sanctis, unus in Veteri Testamento (Exodus 1:5), alter in Novo Testamento (Isaiah 9:1), nomen Rion compositum est ex tribus literis 'R', 'I', et 'O', quae repraesentant verba 'R' (caput), 'I' ( columna vertebralis), et 'O' (articulus), quae iterum iterumque apparet in nomine Dei 'Iesu', nomen Rion sonat ut coniunctio nominum 'Rion' et 'Oen', quae sunt nominata duo animae, 'R' (caput) et 'Iesu' (Deus), qui repraesentant Deum 'Iesu' in forma plura.

in_english.name: Rion
in_english.meaning: son of the river, name of two children in the Bible
in_english.long_meaning: son of the river, name of two children in the Bible, one in the Old Testament (Exodus 1:5) and the other in the New Testament (Isaiah 9:1), the name Rion is composed of three letters 'R', 'I', and 'O', which represent the words 'R' (head), 'I' (column vertebra), and 'O' (articulus), which again appear in the name of God 'Iesu', the name Rion sounds like a conjunction of the names 'Rion' and 'Oen', which are names for two souls, 'R' (head) and 'Iesu' (God), which represent God 'Iesu' in a more complex form.

biblical_reference.note: name of two children in the Bible, one in the Old Testament and the other in the New Testament

data.cultural_impact: The name Rion carries a sense of strength and leadership, evoking the warrior spirit of Celtic tradition. It can be seen as a fitting name for a courageous and determined individual, who is respected and influential within his community.
data.spiritual_significance: From a Christian perspective, the name Rion connects to the image of Jesus as the King of Kings. It serves as a reminder that faith can provide us with the inner strength and authority to rule our lives wisely and justly, just like a king rules a kingdom.

historical_references.reference: Rion, a martyr of the Diocletian persecution (284-305 AD), is said to have been a deacon of the church in Rome. According to tradition, he was denounced for refusing to offer sacrifice to the Roman gods and was brought before the governor of the province. He was tortured and ultimately beheaded. His relics were later interred in the church of San Lorenzo in Lucina in Rome.

Rion, a bishop of Belgrade (Rascia) in the 14th century, was instrumental in spreading the influence of the Franciscan Order in the Balkans. He is also known for his efforts to convert the Serbian population to Christianity and to bring about peace between the various warring factions in the region.
historical_references.context: Spread of Christianity in the Balkans and regional peacekeeping
